subject: Reserve tenor negotiation & start-gate options for SlateWorks
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@slateworks.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved capacity — term & start flexibility

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. We're excited to move forward with Redwood but need clarity on three things before procurement signs off:

1) Term options: Our CFO prefers 12 months but will consider 24 if we get stronger unit pricing. Can you outline the delta between 12/24/36 month pricing at the 50% GPU pool utilization we discussed?

2) Ramp / start date: We have internal infra availability on Sept 1, but can push to Oct 1 if that materially improves pricing. Any flexibility on the start-gate?

3) Credits / onboarding: We need a one-time onboarding credit or invoice milestone tied to capacity activation. What's common for similar customers?

Appreciate a short matrix or bullet list — procurement wants something they can review quickly.

Best,
Dana Li
Head of ML Platform
SlateWorks
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@slateworks.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity — term & start flexibility

Hi Dana — great to hear. Attached is a short pricing matrix and a proposed ramp schedule.

Top-level options (summary):
- 12-month: higher per-GPU price, no long-term commitment discounts. Suitable if SlateWorks expects big changes in 12 months.
- 24-month: ~12% discount versus 12m at target utilization; allows staged ramp over first 60 days.
- 36-month: deepest discount (~20%) with an optional mid-term rebaseline at month 18.

Start gate options:
- Sept 1 start: standard onboarding; first invoice at activation.
- Oct 1 start: we can offer an additional one-off onboarding credit (up to 5% of first-year committed spend) if you sign a 24m+ term.

Onboarding credit & milestones: we typically do a two-step invoice (activation and 30-day). For larger deals we convert the first invoice into a credit applied over the first 3 invoices.

See attached: SlateWorks_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx and Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v3.pdf

If helpful, Ben can put together a formal concession letter for procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: SlateWorks_Ramp_Schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity — term & start flexibility

Quick notes: we should preserve margin but be pragmatic.

Suggested concession structure (if SlateWorks signals urgency):
- Offer 10% one-time onboarding credit for 24m if start = Sept 1 but commit to 70% minimum pool utilization months 1-3.
- If they insist on 12m, offer 6% discount on unit pricing with a $30k activation fee to cover short-term capacity allocation.
- For Oct 1 start, we can extend a 5% extra discount on top of 24m pricing if they accept a 30% prepayment against year 1.

Neha — confirm SLA/throughput guarantees we can promise for their target peak queries per second (I'll forward the estimate). Jonas — need ops note on guaranteed earliest activation window for Sept 1.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Li <dana.li@slateworks.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity — term & start flexibility

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the options. Procurement reviewed and has a couple asks before we go to legal:

- They prefer a 12-month term but are open to 24m if Redwood can provide an activation credit of at least 8% and a firm start date on or before Sept 15.
- If we do 24m, CFO wants a midpoint re-eval clause to renegotiate if our usage is <60% after month 6.

We can share a clean POC-level invoice schedule if that helps. Also, is there flexibility around the minimum pool utilization in months 1-2? We expect initial ramp to 40-50%.

Thanks — I'll be offline tomorrow but back Friday.

Dana

Date: 2027-08-14T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final pricing/capacity proposal & sign path

Dana — appreciate the clarity. Proposed counter to take to procurement (short bullets):

- Term: 24 months.
- Pricing: 12% discount vs 12m list at expected utilization. Applies with a 70% committed pool utilization measured as a trailing 30-day average after month 3.
- Activation credit: 8% one-time credit applied to the first two invoices if start date is on or before 2027-09-15.
- Midpoint re-eval: include a mutual rebaseline at month 12 (not month 6). If actual utilization <50% for months 7-9 we agree to a commercial review and optional adjustments tied to usage (not automatic price reductions).
- Minimums: allow a 45% soft-min utilization window for months 1-2 (grace period) provided they meet 60% for months 3-4.
- Start gate: Sept 15 firm if purchase order received by Aug 20; otherwise default to Oct 1 pricing with no activation credit.

I've attached a redline-friendly one-page concession letter and the ramp schedule. If this matches procurement's needs I can route a DocuSign for signature (link below).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/signer?example=slw_doc_177
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/slateworks-onboarding

Next steps: let me know if procurement accepts the 24m + 8% credit + Sept 15 startgate; I'll send the DocuSign and loop legal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
